utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness. Would you please stand up. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Dragoslav Trisic. My father's name was Stanko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: T-r-i-s-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, July 1995, were you with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what position you held.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was assistant commander for logistics of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long you held that position.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From November 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we talk about your position as the assistant commander for rear services of the Bratunac Brigade, could you please tell us where are you from.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the -- your educational background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the secondary construction school in Tuzla. I attended a school between 1961 and 1965. After that, I graduated from the school for teachers in Tuzla, also -- and I got an associate degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you do your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your service, did you also attend the reserve -- or the academy for reserve officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after completing your JNA service, could you please tell us your -- a little bit about your work background. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: After the compulsory military service, I started working at a school, as a teacher. After that in July 1973, I became chief of the staff of Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality. I was fully employed there throughout my entire career. In the meantime, I was also assistant president of the executive committee for some three or four years, and this was around the year 1980 or 1983. After that, I returned to the Territorial Defence; first I was the chief of the staff of Territorial Defence and then the commander of Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality. And I stayed in that position until the 1st of May, 1991, when I was retired at the age of 44, after 25 years of service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as the commander of the Territorial Defence, could you please tell us a little bit about that, the Bratunac municipality Territorial Defence. How -- first of all, what are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence is a segment of the armed forces of the former Yugoslavia. The armed forces consisted of the JNA and the Territorial Defence. In Bratunac municipality, like in any other municipality of the former Yugoslavia, we had our Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that consist of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the territory of Bratunac municipality, pursuant to regulations, we established staffs and units of Territorial Defence. At the municipality level we had units at the level of detachment and some units attached to the staff. And at local communes, we had local commune units. And all of those units were under the command of the municipal staff of Territorial Defence. We established those units, we equipped them with arms and military equipment, and we trained those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how large was the staff of the Territorial Defence of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As commander of this peacetime staff, I had four associates. I had assistant for operations, assistant for intelligence, assistant for organisation and mobilisation, and assistant for logistics. In addition to that, we also had a few other associates who were handling the equipment, who served as guards, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the ethnic background of the staff members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We always tried to reflect the ethnic composition of the population in the municipality. We always tried to have an adequate representation of all ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, of the four associates, you know, what was the composition, plus yourself, that's five?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Two of my associates were Muslims, two were Serbs, and I am also a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What was the relationship between the Territorial Defence, the TO, of the Bratunac municipality with the professional army, the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The TO was organised across a region. We had a regional staff in Tuzla; they were our superior command. In the territory of Bratunac municipality, we did not have any units of the JNA, so we did not have any particular cooperation with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you were the commander of the Territorial Defence up until 1991. Were you mobilised in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would have been with the Territorial Defence at that point in time, as a result of the war. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and that would have been the Serb Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Serb Territorial Defence, although I was mobilised by the Ministry of Defence, its department, which was formed by the Serbian municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what position did you hold when you were mobilised in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was the chief of staff of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you hold that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: For a very short period of time, until the end of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There were various developments within the command cadre of this organisation. The then-commander, Nikolic, due to problems left the command, some new officers came and joined the command. They joined from the JNA; they took over duties in the command and I was some sort of an operative, an assistant of a sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say Commander Nikolic, we're talking about Momir Nikolic. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the Bratunac Brigade was formed, did you -- were you mobilised within the Bratunac Brigade immediately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what position did you hold then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was appointed assistant commander for logistics, and I remained in that position until the end of war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, prior to that position, did you at any point hold a position within the security organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a while in autumn 1992 I was assistant commander for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just intelligence or was that intelligence and security?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you would have held the same position that Momir Nikolic were to hold once the Bratunac Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if you could please tell us a little bit about your function as the assistant commander for rear services. What does that entail, in general?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, it involves providing security for materiel and equipment that belonged to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say: "Providing security for materiel." What does that mean? Here at one point you're talking about logistics, now you're talking about providing security for the materiel. What exactly you are doing as the commander or the assistant commander for rear services? What do you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I said supplying materiel and technical equipment, ammunition, fuel, food, clothing for the troops, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- now, who was your commander, your immediate commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where do these materiel and technical equipment and the ammunition come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They came via the logistics of the Drina Corps, one part of it. And whatever we couldn't get through them, we obtained through Bratunac municipality. Mostly this was food, fuel, and clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the method by which you would make a request and the supplies would come and what would happen once the supplies arrived.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I would assess the situation. Based on what we had obtained from the corps, I would make an assessment of the situation. And when I realised that some of the things were in short supply, I would make a request to the Executive Board of Bratunac municipality. I would list the quantities of things that I needed, what kind of food, what kind of clothing I needed. I would specify the quantities. At the level of the municipality, there was a staff which was in charge of logistics for the brigade. We would discuss things, and mostly my requests would be carried through and we would agree which company in the territory of Bratunac would supply us with what things. For example, the transport company Vihor, which was the biggest transport company in the municipality, would supply us with fuel and some other things that we couldn't get hold of through other companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about if you had a request to the corps, say for ammunition, what would the procedure be there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I would send a written request according to what I had at my disposal and according to the assessment of the logistics of the corps, I would either receive the quantities that I required or less, depending on what things the corps had at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this assessment that you would make, would you need to get preclearance before sending it off to the corps, or could you just automatically make that request?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation. I could send my request directly to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when supplies arrived, was there a manner in which to keep track of the supplies, what was requested, what was delivered, when it was delivered, to whom, and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had very regular records on materiel and technical equipment received and used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how would you keep track of it? How were the records kept?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We had documents. The so-called records of materiel which served to approve using materiel and technical equipment from the brigade depot. It was my assistant who prepared that, and I was the one who checked those lists and who signed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the assistant, by the way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I had an assistant for technical services, I had an assistant for traffic and transport, and I had an assistant for quartermaster supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I also had an assistant for medical affairs and veterinarian affairs, but subsequently the position of an assistant for veterinarian affairs was abolished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, could you tell us who those assistants were, their names, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The chief of quartermaster supplies was Bozo Momcilovic in 1995. The chief of technical services was Marko, whose last name I can't remember at the moment. The chief of transport services was the late Pavle Loncarevic. The chief of medical services was Ljubo Beatovic. And in 1995, the veterinarian services did not exist in the rear services of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that there was a depot, I take it a warehouse. Is that -- am I correct? Would there have been a warehouse for the Bratunac Brigade for their supplies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, could you please tell us where that warehouse was, the location.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the centre of town where the former warehouse of the TO was. We took the warehouse from them. This is where we had our quartermaster supplies. As for the ammunition, the depot for ammunition was also in town, across the road in the facilities of the tobacco station of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what about for the fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As far as fuel is concerned, we mostly used the Vihor transport company facilities and their petrol station. And if smaller quantities were concerned, up to 200 litres, we kept the supplies in the brigade, in our warehouse in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, where were the records kept, the records for materiel received and materiel consumed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the building of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your office, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: My office was in the Kaolin company building, in its administrative building, on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side? The right, where the commander was; or the left, where Momir Nikolic's office would have been? Which section?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, across the corridor from the office of the commander and the chief of operations' sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, for accounting purposes, when would materiel that had been distributed be considered consumed, at what point in time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: When materiel is issued from the warehouse of the brigade and when it is given for use to subordinate to units, we cross it out from the records of the brigade because we consider that this materiel or equipment has been used and it is no longer part of our supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you receive any documentation or verification from those who had received that materiel, such as for instance ammunition, denoting that it had, in fact, been actually used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We had a document, a so-called materiel sheet, and we had two copies of that. One we retained for our use, and the other, the person to whom materiel would be issued, would take away with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But let me give you a hypothetical, just an example. You issue ammunition to a particular battalion commander. Would that battalion commander at some point in time present you with some sort of written verification that the ammunition that you had given him had been indeed consumed, used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about fuel? Was it any different for fuel, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, for our regular activities we had precise calculations. As to the quantities of fuel required by each unit, for instance, for a period of seven days. So we had sufficient quantities of fuel. We would issue them with seven-day rations of fuel. If we didn't have sufficient quantities, then we issued quantities we did have, and then we would subsequently supply them with the additional quantities of fuel that they needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we get into the events of July 1995, if you could tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That wasn't responsive to your -- to the question. I think you asked if he gave receipts for the fuel. He said how he gave fuel, but didn't whether or not or had to receipt or account for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe your question is not quite clear, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That could be it, Your Honour, that could be very well. I appreciate the assistance. Let me go back before we go on to the next section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you distributed the fuel, did you get some sort of a written accounting, some sort of a report that the fuel you had distributed had indeed been consumed, and if so, how, under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I said, before we get into the events of July 1995, could you please tell us how many vehicles, buses, trucks - transport vehicles I'm referring to - did the Bratunac Brigade own as its own?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We had two buses being used by the brigade to transport its personnel. We had two T-A-M, TAM trucks, 110 and 150. That's the make, or rather, the strength of the trucks. We had two small delivery vans that we called little TAMs, which were 2-ton vehicles. And at the level of our basic units, we had tractors to transport the equipment and food and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, of these two buses, were they owned by the Bratunac Brigade? Were these VRS buses that belonged to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. These were mobilised buses that were mobilised through the national defence department from the Vihor transport company from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the TAM trucks, were those -- you said that there was 110 and 150 TAM trucks. Were they actually owned by the VRS, the Bratunac Brigade, or were they mobilised as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were the property of the VRS, the Bratunac Brigade. In other words, these were typically military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the two small delivery vans that you call "little TAMs," 2-ton vehicles? Were they owned by the VRS or were they vehicles -- were those vehicles that had been mobilised for the use of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: One of these little TAMs was inherited from the Territorial Defence, and the other delivery van, the other little TAM, was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it mobilised from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I really cannot recall at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the Bratunac Brigade needed to transport its soldiers from one location to the other, assuming that it would not be doing so by foot, you know, they would be moving from one location to the other by foot, how would they get there? What were the means of transportation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They would get there by buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which buses? Would the ones that had already been mobilised be used, or would you -- would it require the request of further mobilisation of additional buses from Vihor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They would be transported by already-mobilised buses which were already with the brigade. But if that should prove to be sufficient [as interpreted], we would ask for additional buses from the Vihor transport enterprise. Because we had an agreement with the ministry of defence that we would be able to obtain buses to transport personnel. And after such transport had been carried out, we would return the buses in question immediately to Vihor transport company for their use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one area before we move in to July 1995, and that is the issue of fuel. Could you please tell us what the storage capacity for fuel that the Bratunac Brigade had, and I'm not speaking about Vihor, I'm talking about the brigade itself, the VRS. What storage capacity it owned in Bratunac, if it owned any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We did not have any facilities of our own to store fuel. We just had conventional barrels of 200 litres capacity, so we could store about five to six such barrels. Or in other words, storage about a tonne or a tonne and a half in the brigade storage facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What if the brigade needed additional fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We also had an agreement with the Vihor transport company, and we could store such fuel in the tanks of Vihor, provided, however, that we would issue orders to the effect that that fuel could be poured into the vehicles or the buses or we would be -- we would take, ourselves, several hundred litres in barrels. We would then transport them to our own facility. And then from that facility, we would then tank the cars in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go right into July 1995. First of all, were you on duty during that month?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to use a couple of dates as reference dates, the first date being July 6th, which is when the events surrounding Srebrenica began, and July 11th, the date when Srebrenica fell. All right. First of all, let me ask you: Prior to July 6th, were you asked to make any special provisions in light of the situations that were about to unfold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what those special provisions were. Just in general, and then we'll go into the specifics.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Ammunition and fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, obviously if you were making special provisions, you must have been informed as to what it was needed for. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, perhaps this might be as good a time as any to go into the documents. So -- and perhaps I'm going to start with a little bit before July. And let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D155. First of all, I believe you are being handed a document with the ERN number of 00671801. Do you recognise the handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It is mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... dilemma?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No dilemma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date, could you please tell us what the date is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us -- now, it states here, just for the record, it states: "Requisition of TMS equipment and materiel." And it's being submitted to the Drina Corps. Could you please tell us what is this document about, dated 28th June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is about a requisition of ammunition for a 20-millimetres anti-aircraft gun, an M38. To clarify, Captain First Class Bosko Vukovic was my assistant for the rear in the Skelani battalion, otherwise he, too, had worked earlier in the rear sector of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence. So we were actually acquaintances from before the war and we cooperated. We would supply with each other the lacking materiel and equipment. And in a conversation that we had, I found out that they had such ammunition for the 20-millimetre PAT, the anti-aircraft gun, which was redundant because they did not have such a gun. So we agreed that they would actually give that ammunition to us. In view of the fact that the corps was actually the entity which issued the orders for such issuance and transfer of ammunition, I applied to the corps for them to approve for me taking over ammunition for the 20-millimetre gun from the Skelani battalion, and the amount concerned was 6.000 rounds, bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concretely, did this request have anything to do with the events that were about to unfold with respect to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, since this document has nothing to do with the events in Srebrenica, I fail to see your purpose to introduce this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The whole purpose, Your Honour, is that the Prosecution from day one has argued that this has been a joint criminal enterprise dating way back, which is why I go back to July 4, 1994. This is a document where, for instance, special ammunition is being requested. The argument I anticipate is that even before the events of Srebrenica, before the July 2nd Krivaja 95 order by the Drina Corps and the July 5 order by Colonel Blagojevic, preparations are undergoing for the attack on Srebrenica. And what I want to demonstrate is the -- the dangers of circumstantial evidence, because here's a document that circumstantially we might say, yes, they're gearing up for combat by having the special ammunition, but in effect it's just a coincidence of timing and nothing more. And I anticipate they're going to bring it, so I'm doing a little pre-emptive striking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed. But when we are admitting this document into the evidence, I think we have to consider the relevance. Because this is a document introduced by the Defence, not by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. We may not need to introduce it now that we have an explanation because I'm suggesting that it's not relevant at all, and I don't want to be in a position where on re-direct I'm being restricted from going into this area. So I'm trying to anticipate what documents the Prosecution may be relying on. I think this is a good document that they could circumstantially and legitimately say: Here is some proof. And I'm trying to demonstrate that there's a difference between good circumstantial evidence and bad circumstantial evidence. And this is obviously a good example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me show you what has been marked for identification -- actually has been admitted as P543. And I'm showing you what has come in already as evidence. It's dated July 2nd, 1995. Could you please look at it first of all and tell us whether you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether you had seen this document dating back -- in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I had to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, why do you say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the superior command of the corps command, which is an order for active combat which was submitted to the Bratunac Brigade. And in view of my role, of course I had to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we're going to get to that. Now, is there anything in this particular document that would be of interest or of significance to you, in light of your position as assistant commander for rear services of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please inform us which section might that be.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That is item 9 of this order which refers to rear security, rear support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be on page 8 of the English version, for Madam Usher's convenience. Now, you say -- here it says: "Rear security." And from this section here, can you help us out here, to what extent would this have been useful to you or significant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This was useful it states here that the following quantities of ammunition and fuel were approved to us for the execution of the task as well as other items.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that would be with respect to all the units that were to take place -- were to take part, I should say, in the -- in these activities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and I take it there is a section in this particular document that specifically makes reference to the role that the Bratunac Brigade would be playing in the upcoming activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go on to the next document and we're going to go chronologically or at least date-wise. And now I want to show you what has been marked as 149 -- actually, it has been admitted as 149. If you could look at that. First of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you -- again, you have the actual handwritten version with the ERN number 00671762. Could you please tell us, first of all, do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whose handwriting it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It is my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no dilemma there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at this, could you please explain this to us. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the fact that we had been issued with a preparatory order for the execution of combat operations and as we said in point 9, certain items of technical resources, materiel equipment, were approved for us. Here I made the corresponding request to the corps for them to approve to me to be issued with fuel and ammunition, and I asked for two motor vehicles, because we lacked those, as well as a thousand pieces of dry rations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just so we have a clear record, the first paragraph you state -- pursuant to your preparatory order, and then there is a number of that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we were to go to the previous document, which has been admitted as P543, that should reflect that number, should it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to make sure that we have a clear record. If you could compare the two numbers and tell me if they are actually identical.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The difference is that my document has -1, 156-1, and the Drina Corps document has 156-2. That's the difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're referring to a 156-1, where in fact the Drina Corps document, July 2nd, is 156-2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nonetheless it's your belief that this particular document that you generated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'll let him finish his question, I thank Your Honour. I think I know what he was saying. But he was providing the belief for the witness for him, which is -- which is leading. I also believe we have that preparatory order, which I think is different. I'm not absolutely sure, but I think we do have that preparatory number. They're pretty good with their numbers and I think they got the numbers correct, but that would be some help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this referring to the same document, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now, let me show you some other documents, and please keep that one there, that is D149 for identification. I want to show you some other documents, a series of documents, that come under D166. And we have an unofficial translation, the best we could under the circumstances. And we will get an official translation. And when I say "unofficial," it's -- we have done it -- the Defence has prepared this translation. Now, I'm showing you a series of documents, and they start with the ERN number 00663544 -- actually, some of the numbers are a little off. But in any event, if we could go through these documents one by one. Have you seen these documents before, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, first of all, what these documents purport to be.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This document is, as I referred to it before, the so-called materiel sheet, as it is indicated in the top left corner, according to which we received materiel and equipment from the military post office, military garrison, 7111 in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are these receipts, documentation of actual receipts that would reflect what you physically received, pursuant to your request of 3 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us whether you've had an opportunity to review these documents and then to compare these receipts with your request of 3 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us to what extent these receipts accurately and correctly reflect the request for equipment and materiel you had made to the Drina Corps on 3 July 1995. First give us in general, and then we'll go one by one, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I noticed that the -- that they delivered to us ammunition that we had not asked for in our request of the 3rd of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where would that be, under which -- which kind of ammunition did you receive that was not requested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: For instance, in this first document, the 30-millimetre bullets, we got 240 of those, and that is ammunition for the anti-aircraft gun, the so-called Praga gun, which anti-aircraft gun we did not have. And also, on the same page the 100-millimetre bullet, 30 pieces, that is ammunition for a tank, and we had no -- we didn't have such a tank. Also in the subsequent pages, the other documents, for instance, the document marked D00633542 [as interpreted]. Under serial number 3, they added 100-millimetre PF bullet, we received 30 pieces, 30 rounds. Other -- it is written: According to agreement, Major Basevic. So this is something which was inserted subsequently, obviously. And the likewise, we did not require this kind of ammunition. So that means it was on the basis of some other, somebody else's request, that they actually decided to also deliver this type of ammunition to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what happened to that ammunition that was not requested but was delivered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I assumed that this ammunition was forwarded to some other unit that participated in the operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just for the record, the previous reference to the 100 bullets by Mr. Basevic, Major Basevic, that would be on 166.8, D166.8, at the bottom. All right. Now, of the ammunition that you did request, did all of it arrive pursuant to the receipts that we have here at least?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't arrive, not all of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you go down the list, could you go down the list of the requests that you made and tell us what was asked and what was received.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: For example, we didn't receive fuel. Our request was for 5.000 litres of oil and MB petrol, 2.000 litres. We didn't receive the quantities that we requested. We also didn't receive vehicles, and we didn't receive dry rations. Now, as far as the ammunition is concerned, I would have to make a comparison, but I can say that we received approximate quantities. Some of the things that we requested we got more of, and some of the others that we requested we received less of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me go back to the fuel. You had -- it says here that you made a request for 5.000 litres of diesel. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of that, how much is reflected in those receipts that you received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't have this receipt here, but I believe that we received a lot less, maybe less than 1 tonne of the diesel. And I'm not sure about the MB petrol, but I believe that it was anything between 200 and 400 litres. I don't have the document in front of me that I could consult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if you could look at -- at the top you will see D166.6. It's handwritten.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Yes, I do have it. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how much fuel, diesel, does this reflect that you actually received? You made a request for 5.000; how much did you receive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: 800 litres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And what about petrol? If you could look at 166.7. We know that you requested 2.000 litres of petrol.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received 400 litres. And you can see from this document that they also added bullets for 40 pieces of bullets. And this is very unusual on a sheet reflecting fuel to have ammunition as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you ever -- did you notice that you were receiving ammunition that you had not requested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You noticed that back then? I'm talking about July 3rd or thereafter, when these deliveries were actually made.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I didn't pay too much attention to the ammunition that arrived. The most important thing was that it did arrive. I didn't really pay too much attention to whether the ammunition merely followed my requests or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next set of documents, the next documents, and let me show you what has been entered in as an exhibit as P406. Do you recall ever seeing this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is an order for active combat operations of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there any section in this particular order that directly relates to your section?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Item 11, logistics support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be page 6, Madam Usher, in English. Now, could you please look at these items. First of all, do you know who came up with the actual items and figures?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us in this -- on this list under 11, logistical support, who made -- who came up with this list of items?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And on what basis did you formulate this list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the assessment of materiel and equipment needed for combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at -- if we go down the list, first of all, number one talks about ammunition. And it says --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first part: "Infantry weapons: Two combat sets (for active combat)." What does that mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Means two infantry weapons, combat sets, I forget what it was, but I believe it's 2 times 150 bullets for infantry weapons for active combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- so would that mean that the entire Bratunac Brigade, every soldier received 150 bullets for this operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of them within the Bratunac Brigade would have received this amount?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Only the troops which were engaged in attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at this particular order, can you tell us, at least to your understanding, which troops are we talking about? Which units within the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Under 5 five here. It says: Auxiliary forces will carry out attack on the axis of Pribicevac, and those are the auxiliary units of the 3rd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So, to your understanding, only those units are to receive any additional ammunition, other than what all the other troops already have in their possession?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then if we talk -- then if we go down the list you say: "Artillery and mortars: One combat set." What are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It means that the artillery weapons and pieces, everybody who had them would receive one combat set of appropriate ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many that might be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be sure at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if we go down it says: "T-34 tank: 0.5 combat set." A half a set. Was there a tank within the Bratunac Brigade, a T-34, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As far as I know at that time we didn't have a T-34 tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "at that time," we're speaking of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then we have anti-armour weapons and anti-aircraft weapons. What exactly are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft weapons, that is a 20-millimetre gun, and some anti-armour weapons, that means hand-held rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what -- it says: "0.5 combat set." How many units are we talking about, how many pieces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you repeat the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just rephrase it. Are these large amounts that you're making -- that you're requesting, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, these are not large amounts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to the fuel. Under fuel you say: "Combat vehicles: 0.5 tank of fuel." How much fuel are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Those were minimum quantities, because we didn't have combat vehicles. And even for non-combat vehicles, we didn't request a lot because there were no combat movements carried out by non-combat vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But it says here half a tank, 0.5 tank of fuel. What does that mean? Does that mean half a tank in the vehicle itself or does this reflect something else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Half a tank of the vehicle itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the vehicle -- the vehicles -- the combat vehicles would not even have a full tank of fuel in them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same amount goes for non-combat vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Correct again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then if we look at number 3, you say food -- here it notes that it's: "Cooked food until the beginning of combat operations ..." Could you please explain that to us a little bit.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that according to the order, our troops would mostly secure the line, which means that they would secure the lines reached. That meant that we could prepare cooked food for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just one last question before we perhaps take a break. On number 4 it says here: "Every battalion shall develop a station for logistical support of own forces and provide for the consumption of the above-mentioned quantities of materiel supplies." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This means that every battalion on the basis of the delivered quantities of ammunition, fuel, and food would have to distribute those according to standards, which means that they would have their own logistical support and distribution within their unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would they then provide you with some sort of verification as to what was actually consumed, or once it's distributed, it's outside your hands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Once we delivered to our subordinate units, we lost control of it. And they would distribute those according to their own decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you get verification that it was actually distributed and consumed, in other words, a receipt back saying on this date or during this period we consumed, indeed, what you provided us, so at least you could keep track for your own accounting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, we did not receive any confirmation of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be a good point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break. And we'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me -- before I go into the next document, would you please tell us -- well, let me focus your attention on July 6th and all the way to the 11th. Could you please tell us during that period of time, were any special requests made of you in light of the ongoing activities at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- where were you during that period, from the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, the 10th, the 11th, where were you physically located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to move or relocate your rear services to be closer to the battle activities that were going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during that period of time, do you recall whether you had any particular contacts with your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What was the nature of the contact that you had with him on the 6th of July, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of July, I don't recall having had any particular contacts with him on that day. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the 7th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The commander was mostly in the Pribicevac sector, performing his tasks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you recall whether your commander ever contacted you from Pribicevac requesting you to provide any assistance in light of your position, the period of the 6th to the 11th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever visit any of the front lines during that period or any of the --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us where you went and when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the 9th or on the 10th that I went to the Pribicevac sector, which belonged to the forward command post of the Drina Corps. I went with the president of the executive committee, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell us what were the reasons for going there, at whose request were you going there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: President Davidovic asked me to accompany him in his visit to the command of the Drina Corps in the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you were concerned with respect to you yourself, was this a formal trip? Were you there on any particular capacity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The president wanted to visit the corps command, and I went there just to get an overview of the situation, possibly to control the logistical support of the 3rd Battalion and how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you meet with anybody of the 3rd Battalion to see whether they needed your logistical support?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I met with the officers in charge of the logistics of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were there in the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Who they were?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah. Do you have their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: One of them was Mr. Davidovic's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what, if anything, did you learn?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The situation was just regular. There were no special problems in terms of logistical support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any requests made of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you up there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: An hour, or two hours at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you that entire time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was there around the command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you walk around to -- I believe there's a location up there called Kula. Did you go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't go up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you go to the trenches to see how the men were doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not go to the front line. I was in the vicinity of the command all the time, maybe a couple hundred metres away from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see your commander, Blagojevic, there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I can't recall having seen him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing anyone -- any higher-echelon officers from the corps or from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: General Gvero from the Main Staff of the VRS was there. And I went to see General Gvero, together with Mr. Davidovic. We had a coffee or some drinks. I can't remember exactly, and we talked for a while about the current problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the current problems that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, the activities that were being carried out around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, General Gvero from the Main Staff, do you know what his particular function is there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He was the assistant for morale in Mladic's Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see General Krstic there by any chance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know Bozo Momcilovic? I think I'm pronouncing it correctly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, who is this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Bozo Momcilovic was the chief of the quartermaster corps in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him up there at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was he doing up there in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He had been assigned to be the officer in charge of the rear sector at the Pribicevac forward command post by an order of the command. He was appointed assistant for the rear, i.e., the commanding officer in the logistics sector of the corps and the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point -- prior to that -- if I understand your answer, he's a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At that point in time, was he with the Bratunac Brigade or had he been re-assigned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, he was re-assigned and he discharged obligations at the rear sector of the Drina Corps, at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point in time, who would have been his commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, who ordered him to be with the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic issued that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he issue that order directly to him or do you know whether Colonel Acamovic went to Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, to seek permission whether he could use this gentleman or do you know whether he came to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's leading, offering all kinds of alternatives. The question can be simply asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Colonel Acamovic went to Colonel Blagojevic to ask permission to use this gentleman, who clearly was working in your sector to be with the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Acamovic come to you to ask permission from you whether -- to you -- he could use Bozo Momcilovic to be working for the Drina Corps up there in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Before the start of the combat operations, Bozo Momcilovic went to the official corps command at Vlasenica. There Colonel Acamovic handed to me an order on the engagement in the rear sector in the Pribicevac sector. After Momcilovic returned, he informed me of this order so that I was made aware of the role that he was to play in the rear sector of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to clarify something here. Now, you said that Colonel Acamovic handed you an order of the engagement in Vlasenica. First of all -- I want to go step by step. Did you go to Vlasenica with Bozo Momcilovic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Bozo Momcilovic went by himself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it was at that -- it was while he was there when he was given this order, it was passed on in order for you to -- from Colonel Acamovic for you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before receiving this order from Colonel Acamovic that was being delivered by Bozo Momcilovic, could you please tell us whether Colonel Acamovic contacted you to receive permission from you on whether he could issue such an order or should issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While you were up in Pribicevac, did you have much -- did you have any contact with Bozo Momcilovic? I know you saw him, but did you speak with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know at what point in time Mr. Momcilovic returned back to the Bratunac Brigade, as a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection as to foundation. There's been no suggestion that this person was ever not a member of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll clarify it. I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- it was evidently clear from the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that point in time when Acamovic on his own, without asking you for permission to take away one of your own men and have him working under the Drina Corps, okay? Who was he working for? Was he working for the Bratunac Brigade or was he working for the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Leading and argumentive. He's arguing his case through this witness; that's not proper for direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think somehow the witness has already answered the question before. You may repeat your previous question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Mr. Momcilovic was working under Acamovic, was he taking orders from you or was he taking orders from Colonel Acamovic? Who was his superior officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's asked and answered. We know who he's under the command of, but that's much different than him not being a member of the Bratunac Brigade. These are important distinctions, and that's why I'm objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the issue we are going to solve is the resubordination issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the problem is that we have to find a way to put the question in a correct way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me try again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm -- just for the record, I'm very patient today. I'm willing to spend the next 45 minutes on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when Acamovic issued that order, taking away your resource, was this gentleman working under your command or was he working under Acamovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's my whole point: Taking away the resource, that's an argument. The Prosecution's argument is that one of the reasons you resubordinate is so that you can take advantage of that resource in the Bratunac Brigade so they can work together. This idea that there's this taking away or separation or complete -- it's argumentive. He's free to argue it, but when it's implicit in his questions that's leading and not proper for direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase again. I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time when Acamovic issued that order, were you able to control and direct Mr. Momcilovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please repeat that again for Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. And I hope he doesn't take it out on the witness. He's now shouting at the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not shouting at the witness, Your Honour. This is so ridiculous on the part of the Prosecution. His own witness, Butler - and I have his transcript over here - has talked about this, about the functional relationships, about resubordination, and I find it utterly ridiculous that these objections are being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the transcript correctly recorded what the witness said. There's no need to repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I was hoping that the Prosecution would listen, because obviously we've covered this area, we've covered this ground, on many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during that period of time from the 6th and onwards, where was this gentleman located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was giving him orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Acamovic receive your permission to give this gentleman any orders before issuing the orders to Mr. Momcilovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what point in time did this subordination to the Drina Corps end with respect to Mr. Momcilovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall with precision at which exact point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at the -- for this period, from the 6th to the 12th, did Mr. Momcilovic prepare any written reports for you so at least you would know what he was doing, what orders he had carried out, while he was working for Colonel -- or under, I should say, Colonel Acamovic of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you what has been marked as D131. This has been admitted. First of all, do you recall seeing this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, have you had a chance to look at your statement, the one that you gave after Mr. Blagojevic was indicted and arrested back on 26 November 2001? Have you had a chance to look at the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have you been provided -- have you been provided with a copy of your statement to the Prosecution that you gave in Banja Luka, 26 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You have not been provided by the Prosecution with this copy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That's right, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did the Defence provide you with a copy of your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall whether you were asked about this particular document back on 26 November 2001, some two years after the indictment or so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just while we're at it, before Mr. Blagojevic was indicted in 1999, did the Prosecution ever bother to come talk to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this particular document, it's dated 12 July 1995; first of all, do you see your name on it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No dilemma?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the first line. It says here: "We hereby submit consumption of materiel and equipment for the period from 10 to 12 July 1995." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain what that means.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: What that means is that in that period from the 10th to 12th, we issued from the storehouse of the brigade to the subordinated units the indicated quantities of materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, does that mean that this materiel was actually consumed, used by the Bratunac Brigade, as this document would have us -- at least it would appear from the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It means that the indicated quantities of ammunition were submitted by us to the subordinated units, and that the level of the stocks of such ammunition in the storehouse of the brigade was reduced by the quantities indicated. What happened afterwards we did not know because we did not get any feedback, any reports on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean that the ammunition was actually used or spent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether you told this to the Prosecution so at least they would know it, back on 26 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, let me show you -- but before we go on to the next document, let's talk about July 11th. That was the day that -- July 11th, 1995, the day that Srebrenica fell. Could you please tell us whether you had any particular requests, in light of your position on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me show you a document that has been marked as P427 -- actually, I believe it has been admitted. All right. Have you seen this -- do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is an order of the command of the Drina Corps -- or rather, the commander General Zivanovic, to the effect that all available buses and minivans which were the property of the VRS units should be made available to the command of the Drina Corps on the 12th in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to go step by step. First of all, we know that the date is 12 July 1995. Do you know approximately what time this document would have arrived at the Bratunac Brigade? Is there anything there that might be able to help you out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see on the document that it was received on the 12th of July at 0835 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, if we were to look at the document in Srpski, which is with the ERN number 00761238. It even states in there - which hasn't been translated - but it states in there who received this document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, could you please tell us who received it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Major Peskic [as interpreted]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be Major Eskic, with an E?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Major Eskic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Major Eskic was in charge of personnel affairs in the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this particular day, looking at this document, looking at where his name is, could you please tell us whether he was carrying out any particular function within the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He was on duty on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can see -- you can tell that from looking at this particular box that's at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could just tell us what the normal procedure would be when a document like this comes in. What would the duty officer do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a small --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- Foundational objection. I think he testified that the person was on duty. I think there's another question to really sort of identify what that means in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what a duty officer is? You told us -- okay. We're going to go step by step. We're not military, so we don't know anything about how the military functions. You indicated that Major Eskic was the duty officer. First of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not what he said, at least in the translation, and that was my point. And so if the question was: "What was his job," that's fine. He said Eskic was on duty -- frankly being on duty, all the soldiers are on duty. Again, I don't -- I think it just needs to be clear. Because all I got in the translation was that his name on this document showed that he was on duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
