utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we could go step by step.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In looking at this particular document, sir, do you know what function he was carrying out on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He was the duty officer at the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, as the duty officer on that particular day -- well, first of all, do you know what those functions are, what are duty officer does, in general? Do you know the functions, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in general, could you please tell us what the duty officer would have done with this kind of a document once it came in to the brigade, what the normal procedure would be.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As this is an order which has to do with a rear sector, he could have passed that order on to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would that order be passed on to you physically or orally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He would have passed it on to me physically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether on that particular day, July 12, 1995, sometime in the morning, whether you received this document? Do you have any recollection of actually receiving the document and looking at it and reading it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, actually I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the procedure would be that it would be passed on to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Now, if we look at this document in a little greater detail, perhaps you might be able to help us out here. I want to focus your attention to the second paragraph -- actually, it's two paragraphs in yours, but the first paragraph of your paper. It says there: "All the available buses and mini-buses belonging to the units of the Army of Republika Srpska must be secured for the use of the Drina Corps command on 12 July 1995." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us again, refresh our memories, how many buses and mini-buses belonged to the Bratunac Brigade, to the Army of the Republika Srpska, in order for them to be turned over for usage by the Drina Corps on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We did not have buses which were the property of the Bratunac Brigade. We had two buses that had been mobilised from the Vihor transport company and which were being used by the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you -- so in other words there were no buses to be given to the Drina Corps on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you didn't have any buses that belonged to you, to the Bratunac Brigade, how many would you have been able to give belonging to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. It assumes facts in evidence. I mean, being mobilised, that -- unless he wants to establish that mobilising the buses has no reference at all to the brigade that is mobilised, then that question doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to the second -- Your Honour, first of all, first of all, the gentleman can clear this matter up on cross-examination. But second of all, there is the third paragraph that talks about mobilisation, buses available to state from private owners. And if the gentleman could be a little calmer and more patient, we can get to that. But right now I was talking about belonging - ownership - versus mobilisation and use - usage. And we covered that earlier, and so now I'm going through this step by step, this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have some difficulties with the witness's answer and you may ask some questions to clarify that answer. Because I believe your question should be focused around the answer the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, reading this document where it says: "All available buses and mini-buses belonging to the units of the Army of Republika Srpska must be secured for usage of the Drina Corps." To your understanding, could you please tell us this word "belonging," what is your understanding of it, of this word?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That means the ownership, that they belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Army of the Republika Srpska own buses and mini-buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about mobilise for the usage of; I'm talking about actually owning them.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska had buses. The Bratunac Brigade did not have any buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's look at the next paragraph, because the next paragraph reads: The corps command has sent a request to the ministry of defence of Republika Srpska demanding that the ministry of defence offices in Sarajevo and Zvornik obtain by 12 July 1995 all the buses available from the state and private owners for the use of the commands of the brigades and whose areas the buses are being sought. And then it goes on. In Bratunac, where were those buses coming from that would be available from state and private owners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From all the neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Bratunac itself, was there a state-owned enterprise that had buses and mini-buses that it could lend or let the Drina Corps commandeer or mobilise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which company was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The Vihor transport company from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to show you another document, and this is exhibit P470. Can you read this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is an interim combat report, is it not, dated 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it states here that: "Today" -- that would have been 13 July 1995, "at 1700 hours, we sent a unit consisting of 92 soldiers, led by the chief of staff, to carry out the following tasks in the area of Bracan. The unit was sent on the direction of Bratunac-Milici-Bracan." Now, my question to you, sir, is, first of all: Do you recall soldiers being sent in that direction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I do indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how they would have been transported from Bratunac to this new location.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were transported by two buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which buses are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The buses that were at the disposal of the Bratunac Brigade, which had been mobilised by the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are the same two buses that we have been talking about more or less this morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is July 13, 1995. Let me take you back a day. On 12 July 1995, were those buses that the Bratunac Brigade had mobilised from Vihor, were those buses used in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who issued those orders for those buses to be used.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was in contact with Colonel Acamovic most often, and he made me aware of the fact that on the order of the commander of the Drina Corps we should engage these buses for the transport of Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was on the 12th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if they were being used for that purpose, is there any reason why you didn't go back to Vihor to ask for additional transport to enable the Bratunac Brigade soldiers on the 13th to go to Milici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: When the buses returned from their route towards Kladanj, I talked to my assistant for transport and I asked him to retain the buses which would be used for the execution of the following tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, since we're on the 12th, I want to stay on the 12th before we go to anymore documents. Would you please tell us on that particular day, July 12th, 1995, the day after Srebrenica fell, what you did.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was at the brigade command performing my regular duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that particular day do you recall whether you had any meetings with your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend any meetings where General Mladic was present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, yes, I did go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us first of all who ordered you or instructed you or suggested to you that you go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. It's not helpful to provide three different versions, because we don't know which three would have been used. And it also -- there should be a foundation: Were you ordered to go to Potocari? Not assuming he was ordered to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ordered to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I received an order to organise the preparation and distribution of bread for the Muslim population in the Potocari sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did -- were you ever ordered by anyone to also go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did anyone suggest to you that you should go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone instruct you to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then why did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness answered that question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, he said he was ordered to prepare the bread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we heard why he actually went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To prepare the bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the distribution of this bread to the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't quite clear -- I agree with you, Your Honour, but I want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Potocari -- first of all, could you please tell us: How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I went there by car, but by my own official car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I went there on my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the bread? Was that with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. The bread had arrived in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did it arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was delivered in the mini TAM vehicle that we had at the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time do you recall you went to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Around 11.00 or 12.00, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long you stayed there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: An hour or so, an hour and a half maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what, if anything, you did while you were there for that hour, hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very simply, I was observing the event, the Muslims that gathered there. They were being separated by the soldiers of the DutchBat from the soldiers of the Republika Srpska Army. In the meantime, the bread had arrived. We distributed this bread to the Muslim population. Actually, it wasn't us but the rear company of the Bratunac Brigade that did the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The job being the distribution of the bread?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you were observing the events and that there was DutchBat and also soldiers of the RS. Could you please tell us from which units were these soldiers from the RS, if you know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There were soldiers from units of the Drina Corps. I can't be more precise than that, because I didn't pay too much attention to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that because of the uniforms, that you recognised them to be from the VRS, the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. How did you recognise them --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you recognise them? How did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The troops of the VRS had a certain kind of uniform, of course, but I knew that they were from other units because I didn't know them. Some of them even had an insignia indicating that they belonged to, for example, the Zvornik Brigade. For example, their insignia were wolves from the Drina River. That's what I recognised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about MUP? Did you see any MUP units there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There were also policemen, but not as a unit. Just policemen in police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about special police, special police units? Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Special police, are you referring to the civilian special police or the military police?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the civilian special police.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice any members of the civilian special police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how they were dressed, what colours they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They had different uniforms. As far as I can remember, members of the special police wore black overalls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you see any members of the Bratunac Brigade there, whether they were soldiers or military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There were members of the Bratunac Brigade there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall what they were doing, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, at that moment they were providing security. They were engaged in separating soldiers from the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see any higher-echelon officers there, anybody from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: General Mladic was there; I saw him. General Krstic as well. And there were some other officers from the corps, from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in your statement telling the investigators in Banja Luka that you had been with him that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could -- that's vague. "Having been with him," I think --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the investigators that you had seen him there in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you saw General Mladic, were you able to hear what, if anything, he was saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could hear him addressing the Muslims who were present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please tell us what you heard.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There were women, children, and elderly people there, and he told them not to be afraid. He told them that all who wanted to be transported by buses to Kladanj would be transported there, and that from there they would proceed towards the territory under the control of the -- Alija Izetbegovic's army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe General Mladic when he was telling people not to be afraid, and those who wanted to be transported would be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Because he was talking to women, children, and elderly, to the helpless, starving people. And there was no reason for me not to believe General Mladic's words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While you were there, at that point in time, when General Mladic was speaking to the crowd, did you witness any separation being done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you walk around into the crowd all around that area to see what, if anything, was happening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't move about too much. It was impossible to do that. The population had been separated. I could not have wandered into the crowd. I was standing on the other side of the separation line, and I was just observing what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you spent that hour, and an hour and a half there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I returned to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to the brigade command, did you report to your commander what you had been issued to do by Mr. Acamovic; that is, the distribution of bread?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having reported to him. I did not deem it necessary at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report to him that you had left your post that is at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters and had ventured into Potocari on July 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write any reports to your commander so that at least perhaps he would have something in writing as to what you saw, what you observed, what you heard while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. There was no need for me to issue any special reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, earlier you said that, and we discussed this, that the two buses that had been mobilised from Vihor and were being used by the Bratunac Brigade were now engaged in Potocari pursuant to the request from Mr. Acamovic. Did you inform --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform Colonel Blagojevic that Acamovic had issued the order to you or passed along the order to you that we saw from major -- from General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't inform him about that. I believed that the -- any order issued by the Drina Corps had to be executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know Mr. Acamovic before this, these events? Had you worked with him before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to go into some documents with respect to fuel, and it might take a little while to get through these documents. So this might be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break. And we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, I now would like to go through a series of documents with respect to the issue of fuel. If I could show you -- first of all, we're going to go step by step. I'll just show you what has been -- D156. This is marked for identification as D156. First of all, I want you to look at it very carefully. And as I understand, you're looking at the handwritten version with the ERN number 00671770. First of all, do you recognise this handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It is the late Pavle Loncarevic, who was my assistant for transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look all the way to the bottom, sir, of the page, do we not see your name, assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, that is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there anything there that would reflect that your name is being signed or placed there by someone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There was my associate who wrote my name there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he say "za," for instance, "for," when he signs your name, that he's signing for you? Do you see that there anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go through this document step by step, we see that this would appear to be a report with respect to the consumption of fuel, lubricants, et cetera, for the month of July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, under 1 it says: "Fuel received 1 July 1995." And it states here: "Diesel" -- no. I'm sorry. "Fuel reserves 1 July 1995." Correction. Now, in the reserves it would appear -- of the Bratunac Brigade there were 903 litres of diesel and 148 litres of petrol. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go to the next item. It says: "2. Amounts of fuel received in the course of the month." And we see from the Drina Corps that the Bratunac Brigade would have received, according to this document, 18.300 litres of diesel and 2.160 litres of petrol. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your estimation and having been the assistant commander of rear services for the Bratunac Brigade from the end of 1992 to this point in time in 1995, would this amount, 18.300 litres of diesel and 2.160 litres of petrol, would that be a representative amount of fuel that the Bratunac Brigade would consume on a normal basis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be high or would that be low?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Much more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now we go to subsection b, 2(b). It says that the Bratunac Brigade also received from Vihor 1.684 litres of diesel. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From another company called Gradina, 1.050 litres of diesel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bratunac municipality, 1.000 litres of diesel and 400 litres of petrol.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we see from UNHCR, the United Nations, 30.000 litres of diesel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then from the Eastern Bosnian Corps in Bijeljina, 200 litres of petrol. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if we go now to number 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, everything is written there. Do you need to go over from the very beginning to the end of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may just pose your question to this witness. I don't think there's any disputes concerning what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. Of course, that is not his handwriting; that is somebody else's handwriting. And at some point I'm going to go through these receipts. And I don't want to draw any objections with respect to foundation, lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may ask a general question to this witness concerning with this document. Then they're followed by other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would appear here, sir, that July 1995 the Bratunac Brigade consumed 52.570 litres of diesel and 2.799 of petrol. My question is: Did the Bratunac Brigade consume that amount of diesel and petrol in the month of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It could not have spent this quantity of fuel, but this is the quantity of fuel which was entered in the records maintained by the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to go to that. Did the Bratunac Brigade have the materiel, the transport materiel, to consume such a large amount of diesel and petrol?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we go into the sheets, could you please give us an explanation about these figures. To your understanding, what do these figures represent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: These figures represent as regards item 2(a) and (b). The quantities of fuel which, entered on the basis of valid documents, the rear sector, or rather, the rear company of the Bratunac Brigade. Under 3 are shown the quantities of fuel which went out on the basis also of pertinent documentation from the rear company of the Bratunac Brigade. So these are the incoming and outgoing quantities of fuel, which does not at all mean that it was all spent, consumed, at the time in question for combat or non-combat vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us to the best of your knowledge who consumed, first of all, who consumed this fuel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was the rear sector of the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the rear sector or rear services of the Drina Corps command need to ask permission from you or from your commander in order to consume this fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, given that we're dealing with some fairly large amounts of fuel, could you please tell us, first of all, how that fuel was brought to the Bratunac Brigade, if you know; and two, where it would have been stored.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As regards this first item under (a), in item 2, from the command of the Drina Corps, the fuel would be delivered in the tanks owned by the corps. And these tank trucks were parked on the parking lot of the Vihor transport enterprise, which is at the entry to Bratunac if you look from the direction of Konjevic Polje. So these tank trucks were parked there, and the fuel would be discharged directly from the tanks and the buses would be filled directly there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right here for a second before we go to the next. Who was actually doing that physically?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Physically, the operation was carried out by the driver and the co-driver from the headquarters from the command of the Drina Corps, who were actually driving or operating these tank trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the fuel then put into the buses or trucks that needed fueling at the time? Who was engaged in that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a -- the head of the transport services of the Drina Corps was there, Krsmanovic. I believe that he was a colonel. And this I was informed about by my assistant for the transport service, Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the men from the Bratunac Brigade were involved under the direction of Mr. Krsmanovic in carrying out these tasks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's compound. Were they involved, and then I think then you can ask. But otherwise, it's really not a helpful question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's okay. That's all right. Trial advocacy 101.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the men of the Bratunac Brigade involved in any of these activities; that is, putting the fuel into the trucks and to the buses, if you know? Don't speculate. Don't assume. If you know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what did Mr. Loncarevic, who was working under you, what did he tell you with respect to Mr. Krsmanovic who was from the Drina Corps, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In fact, there was nothing that he had to report to me about specifically, because these were jobs that we had to carry out in view of the presence of the superior command of the Drina Corps on the premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krsmanovic, in which sector of the Drina Corps was he working in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The transport service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the transport service, in which sector is located within the Drina Corps? Who is his commander, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so the transport would be within the rear services. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Krsmanovic seek your authority or permission to use those facilities and use any of your men, if they were engaged, in the distribution of the fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, he did not seek any approval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they at least -- did he at least give you some information that he was about to be carrying out those activities at that location and perhaps might be using some of your personnel in carrying out these activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In fact, we hadn't even met or seen each other at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you by any chance inform your commander, Colonel Blagojevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, that's nonresponsive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krsmanovic there during those days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from Mr. Krsmanovic those days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you hadn't heard from him, you couldn't have received any information from him directly. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just refresh our memory. Who told you about Mr. Krsmanovic being there at that location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: My assistant Loncarevic did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us: When did he tell you? Was this before the activities were carried out? During? Or after?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was after the activities had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these activities were carried out, and once you learned from Mr. Loncarevic that Mr. Krsmanovic, who was working under Mr. Acamovic, was there, did you by any chance then inform your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, as to what had occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There was no need for that, because these were activities carried out or normally carried out by the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's get back to where we were earlier before I interrupted you and we went down this little detour. The other amounts of petrol are rather small until we get to the amount by UNHCR, 30.000 litres of diesel. Could you please tell us, first of all, how did that arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic informed me of the fact that we, the army, would be getting 30.000 litres of fuel, and he asked me whether we had the necessary storage facilities for that. I suggested to him that we should temporarily store the fuel in the tanks of the warehouse -- in the warehouse of the Vihor transport company from Bratunac, and that is the way it was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that fuel ultimately -- how that fuel was ultimately consumed and by whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: A portion of this fuel was used to fill the tanks of the buses used to transport the Muslims. A second part was repossessed by the corps, that is to say these quantities of fuel that had been delivered were practically returned -- in fact, they were returned to the corps so that we actually managed to carry out the entire transportation with the fuel that we received from the UNHCR and the DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," are we talking about the Bratunac Brigade? Who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I mean the rear services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say that "we were able to carry out the entire transportation," are we talking about the we, the Bratunac Brigade, the rear services within the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's leading. It's a who, not trying to exclude the Bratunac Brigade, which is what's going on here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who carried out -- who was carrying out this activity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The rear services of the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- by the way, were you consulted beforehand as to whether they should be over there in Bratunac using your facilities? Did they seek permission from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you ask Mr. Acamovic, you know, for his order, who had ordered him over there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a particular reason why you didn't ask Mr. Acamovic to produce to you some sort of order that would authorise him to be there, taking up your space, perhaps even engaging your men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: By virtue of his position, it is actually Colonel Acamovic that -- who issues orders to me. I have no right to ask him who he received his orders from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would the resources that were consumed from the Bratunac Brigade of such a nature that you would have required -- you would have been required to contact your own commander because perhaps it would have been a disruption in the functional relationship that exists within your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I did not have to consult the commander. These were small quantities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you a list of documents that go along with this. The first series, it's 157, what has been marked for identification as D157. Could you look at that document. Again, this is an unofficial translation. There are actually three documents. First of all, do you recognise these documents, sir, D157, page 1, page 2, page 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell me: What are they? What do you recognise them to be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: These are documents which are evidence of the delivery in three instances on the 12th of July of fuel to the Bratunac Brigade, as this document says, as it is addressed to VP 7042, and that is the Bratunac Brigade. The order for the delivery of fuel is by Colonel -- or I presume Lieutenant Colonel Basevic of the technical service of the Drina corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us the amounts in these three pages from D157? What are the amounts -- the total amounts of fuel you would have received on 12 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The total amount was 13.000 litres of diesel and 400 litres of petrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you could see that from these -- from these three documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, let me show you another document, 158. Do you know what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This document is proof that from the UNHCR Srebrenica we got 30.000 litres of diesel on the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is that the 30.000 that we're talking about in the previous document that we see, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just for the record, we have heard from a Major Franken -- or Colonel Franken, I believe he's colonel right now. He had indicated that to his understanding that the fuel was approximately 27.000 litres and that it had arrived on the 15th or 16th of July. And I'm reading, just for the record, on page 1.490 where he's being questioned by Mr. Waespi, Monday, 15th September 2003. Is Mr. Franken correct in stating that it was about 27.000 litres of diesel and that it had arrived on the 15th or 16th? Or would this document that I've shown you perhaps be more accurate? Which of the two, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The quantity was recorded as 30.000. And I wish to adhere by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And the receipt again on this particular day shows that it was the 13th of July. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me show you the next document, which is D159 for identification. If you could please look at that. Do you recognise this document, sir, or do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I recognise this document. It represents the entry of fuel from the Bratunac Brigade via the (UNHCR) into the Vihor tank. The assistant director of Vihor, Mr. Gojko Stjepanovic, who has signed here in the middle of the page, recorded 23.300 litres of diesel that entered the Vihor tank from the UNHCR. And the owner, according to this document, is the military post 7042.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what post is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us -- it says here: "Received" -- I note here on one of the pages that it says, at least in the handwriting version -- the handwritten version, that what was received from UNHCR was 23.300. Do you know what happened to the rest? Assuming that 30.000 came in, it would appear that some is missing or gone missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's assuming that this is a reference to the other 30.000. There's been no link there. Not that I see a whole lot of relevance, but there's been no indication of a link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could look at the date on this particular document. Now, previously I showed you the actual receipt that says it was from the UNHCR, and we said it was dated 13 July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could look at this particular date, please tell us what is -- what date is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The documents speak for themselves. If this person knows there's a link, we can ask him. But we can see the documents, but there's lots of evidence coming in from places on various dates, and if this person can sort it out, fine. But I don't think we just need to repeat the documents all over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, it's obvious that there's two different figures of the fuel supplied by UNHCR. You may ask a question to this witness whether he knows the difference and what's the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was trying to do that before the objections that were being raised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the arguing with the Court. It's offering more information and unnecessary information to the witness and it's just going to delay the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the delaying of the case, Your Honour, is that the Prosecution has chosen seven years later to begin doing their investigation. I should not be blamed for their incompetence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's come to this specific issue. We did not characterise whose fuel as missing. We just say, obviously there's a difference; what's the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, why there is a difference? On the one hand it says that fuel was received on the 13th with -- from the UNHCR at 30.000. And here in this handwritten note we see that it's only 23.300. Can you account for that difference?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I can assume that before this fuel entered the Vihor tank we had consumed some 6.700 litres. And that the chief accountant at Vihor had -- recorded that immediately and recorded a subsequent entry of 23.300 litres of fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you another series of documents. If we could stick with that document for one more second. If you could look at the handwritten version, that would be on page 2 in the typewritten version in English, at some point it says -- we have a distribution list and it says: "Distributed fuel truck, 13.000," and then again "2.000." Do you see that? In the handwritten version --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us: What does that mean, as far as you understand it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This means that this fuel was again taken over by the rear services of the Drina Corps. This fuel was basically returned to the corps from the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how was it returned or distributed? It says "fuel truck" versus "barrel" further down. What's the distinction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The first entries, 13.000 litres is a big tank; 2.000 is for small tanks. That's the next two items. And the difference was transported in barrels, because there was no more room in either the big tank or the few smaller tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could look at D160, what's been marked for identification as D160. There again is a series of documents. There is a typed version and there is a handwritten version, handwritten being 162. But first let's stick with the D160. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this has the ERN number for the record 00663506. What is this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is the record of fuel which was filled in the buses. Mostly the buses which had been mobilised. You can tell by the registration plates, the numbers on the registration plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were those buses filled, what location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the Vihor parking lot, at the very entrance to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please describe the manner in which these buses would have been filled or these vehicles would have been filled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- form of the question. "Would have been" is not helpful; that doesn't tell us much. If he knows how they were filled or whatever, but "would have been" doesn't tell us anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just ask a direct question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the buses were filled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Directly from the tank. The buses were filled directly from the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "the tank," is that the tank that is located in the ground or outside, or is it the truck that's carrying the fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From the lorry tanks, through the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. Let me show you now D161. This is a very similar document, but perhaps you could just for the record please tell us what it is. The Srpski version is 00663510. Do you recognise this document, or do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I recognise this document, and this represents the quantities of fuel that were filled in various vehicles, lorries and such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were fueled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Again, this was probably done in the Vihor parking lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you one last document. We don't have a translation, although it is just a bunch of numbers. If we could put one on the ELMO. And this document, again provided to us by the OTP, 00663512, marked for identification as D162. Do you recognise this document, or do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I recognise it. This is again an overview of fuel that was put in various vehicles, mostly belonging to the VRS on the 15th of July, 1995, in Borkovac [phoen]. Now, Borkovac is this Vihor parking lot that I have been mentioning all this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on this page we also see the initials "ZV." What does that stand for, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Those are civilian trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I notice the record says 15 July, and I think the document says 13. And unless I'm not seeing something that the witness is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's the witness's answer. You may clarify this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at the top of the document, sir, could you please tell us what the date is on that date.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: 13 of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And this would -- so what again does this represent? I'm not leading you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July fuel was filled in the here-listed vehicles in Borkovac, in the Vihor parking lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That will be it for the fuel. Perhaps I can -- I apologise. If we could go back to just to make sure I clarify one point on D156. Now, we note -- we started by saying that the fuel reserves on July 1, diesel 903 litres, and petrol 148 litres. On this document, does it reflect how many reserves were left at the end of July; that is, it would have been August 1, the next accounting period? Actually, if you go down to number 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: 367 litres of diesel and 109 litres of petrol is what was left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I just wanted to make sure that we covered that point. Now, to other matters. If I could show you what has been marked as -- I'll show you two documents, actually. I just want to start off with D163 for identification, I believe. Yes, D163 for identification. The document is dated 24 July 1995. Do you see your name on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're looking at the handwritten version, are you not, with the ERN number 00671767?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I am indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: My own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that your signature down there at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No dilemma?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No dilemma whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, here it talks about -- this particular document makes reference to certain equipment or property that was appropriated, does it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it was not appropriated rated, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. This list of equipment, that's 1 through 9. Where was this equipment located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was in the possession of the rear service of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But where was it located initially before it was taken into the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Everything between 1 and 8 is the equipment of the Dutch Battalion. Under 8 and 9, those are two civilian trucks which were brought from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of this document, of generating this particular document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The corps wanted us to submit a report on all the collected equipment from the former enclave of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how some of this equipment came into the possession of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Under 1, armoured personnel carrier, six items. We came into the possession of these directly through the crews of the carriers. The DutchBat soldiers would come to the command with their carriers to surrender; that was in two or three cases. And the other two or three surrendered at various checkpoints directly to the military police. The rest of the equipment from 2 through 9 was collected all over the place where Dutch -- the DutchBat had its points. Once those checkpoints were deserted, we collected the equipment -- I'm talking about generators, tents, receptacles for transporting food and so on and so forth. As for the trucks, we got them in Potocari and took them over from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you a document that was generated by Colonel Jankovic approximately -- it was 14 July 1995, very early hours, 0030. This is a report to the command of the Drina Corps' intelligence department. First of all, did you know Colonel Jankovic? Did you know of him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I saw him in Bratunac at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any association with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on this document it says at one point towards the bottom that: "The MUP, Ministry of the Interior, is stealing on a massive scale from UNPROFOR," and it goes on. My question to you, sir, is: Any of the documents -- any of the items that are listed on this particular document that I showed you previously, D163, that you listed, were those stolen by the Bratunac Brigade from UNPROFOR, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, they were not stolen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. When you were in Potocari on the 12th, what did you think was going to happen to the people that were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any reason to give it a second thought. Mladic promised the population that they would be transported to Kladanj. There was no other solution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you there sort of assisting in the ethnic cleansing of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. The Muslims who were gathered there expressed their wish, as far as I know, to be transported to Kladanj. And from there on to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what has happened to some of the men that were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard about any atrocities having occurred after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Later on I did, but at the moment I knew nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you please tell us at least what you have learned since then.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Later on I learned, I heard, that people had been killed, that Muslims had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While you were in Potocari, did you see any separation of men. At the time that you were there, did you notice men, able-bodied men? I'm not talking about the children, I'm not talking about the very old men, did you see any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you asked this question before. We could go back to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm -- as I was asking the question, Your Honour, I realised that I had asked the question, but I was midstream. But thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from what you were able to observe, from what you were able to observe, it appeared to you at the time you were there that the Muslims were being treated correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how can you say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: There wasn't any maltreatment. People, women and children and the elderly started to board the buses. They were not being mistreated. We gave them the little food that we could. Everything proceeded in a regular fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's what you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that at one point prior to you becoming a member of the Bratunac Brigade you were in the intelligence and security sector of the Territorial Defence. Do you remember that? Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who filled that position in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Captain Nikolic did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understood your testimony correctly, when you were working for the Territorial Defence - and if I recall Captain Nikolic's testimony, he would have been there working with you at the same time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to fast forward to July 12th, 13th, and so on. During that period of time, did Captain Nikolic tell you that he had been appointed the coordinator of the units that were in Potocari at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were there did you see him by any chance coordinating among the various units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, he was there and he was doing the work, and that is it, coordination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you that he had been appointed by any chance by Colonel Jankovic to carry out this activity?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a form of argument. The proper question is: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if he didn't tell him anything, then he can argue that, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's part of the evidence and it's part of the Prosecution's case, having believed the gentleman, that is Nikolic, that Jankovic put this captain in charge of coordinating. And I'm merely asking if Momir Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the argument is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There needs to be foundation to a question like that. Because if there is a reason for it, you can see from the foundational question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic ever tell you that on the morning of the 12th Popovic and Kosovic told them that they were going to kill all the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. The foundational question is: Did Mr. Nikolic tell you anything? Mr. Karnavas knows this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know this. This is perfectly normal. I mean, I'm asking whether he was told about the killings. Momir Nikolic came here and testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, we don't know the background, the situations there, whether the witness had that talk with Mr. Nikolic or not. Or maybe he just saw him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Mr. Nikolic during the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I have no recollection of any such talk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these events were over, did Mr. Nikolic ever tell you anything about his involvement, the role that he played with respect to coordinating or assisting in the killings, that sort of stuff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me -- let's go further ahead to October 16, 1995. Let me show you a document that is marked D165. Now, according to this document here, it appears that on this particular day Mr. Nikolic at a meeting, a working meeting of commanders, indicated that he was currently, that is back then, he was engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska General Staff and in parenthesis it says "asanacija." Now, if we look at this piece of paper, do you see your name anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that I was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is this -- do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is Nikolic's handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall being at that particular meeting, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please tell us whether -- from your recollection what discussions were carried out with respect to this particular information, assuming that discussions were held.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't exactly talk. Captain Nikolic was -- informed us that these obligations were being carried out according to orders from the Main Staff. And as for this clean up, this sanitary operation, there were no comments made on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever become aware of any efforts that were being made by the VRS for the reburial process?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware of any activities by the VRS with respect to reburying, removing the bodies and then reburying them in various locations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of any such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you now another document, and this would be the last. I'm going to show you a document that has come here before, that's D132. It's been admitted into evidence. And it's an information from the then-commander Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic, dated 4 July 1994. First of all, could you please tell us whether you recall ever receiving this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Foundation. Before getting into a document, it's proper for him to ask about the subject matter. And if the witness needs refreshing, recollection or anything like that, that's the appropriate -- the proper way to do it. You don't just give people documents on direct and start doing this. It's improper. And I have no objected because I know the rules here can be a little different, but this is -- the proper way to do it, I think, is what ought to be done in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question in my mind is: What is this document to do with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, he was an assistant commander of the rear services at the time, so he would have been in -- one of the higher-echelon officers, shall I put it, within the brigade. The Prosecution has maintained throughout and continues to maintain that this genocidal plan existed way before the campaign against Srebrenica, and particularly with respect to the issue of forcible transfer. The Prosecution intends to argue, I believe - and I think I have a good-faith basis to believe that - that this document demonstrates that there was an ongoing policy by the Bratunac Brigade. They further intend to argue that Mr. Blagojevic, when he took over of the Bratunac Brigade, was carrying out a policy --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is inappropriate to be signalling in this manner --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think if we could be reminded. I'm sure that the Court knows what this document is, and that this man was on duty at the time. And I have no objection to Mr. Karnavas asking questions about it, but to go on and to signal the whole theory of his case and misstating the Prosecution's is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Put this document to the witness. And if you have any questions, you may ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has cited this document in its indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's not relevant what the Prosecution says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It certainly is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He seems to be making it in some way personal, which is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hardly personal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think this is the last document, and you just put your question to this witness concerning with this document. Let's finish today's sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of your position as an assistant commander, or one of the assistant commanders in the Bratunac Brigade, do you recall ever seeing this document from your commander, your then-commander, Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic? And if you don't recall, that's okay. But do you recall --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The last time we did this, I think we heard the answer. And it's -- look at his eyes. He knows what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to help out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ask a question and let's finish this sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing this document ever?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you see it back then when it was generated; that is, in 1994?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct your attention to paragraph number 2 where there's some language there with respect to the enclave of Srebrenica. All right. Where it says, and this would be the last paragraph on paragraph number 2. On the English version it's page 3. I'm going to read just a portion of it. It says: "We must attain our final goal, an entirely Serbian Podrinje, the enclave of Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde must be defeated militarily." And then it goes on: "We must continue to arm, train, discipline, and prepare the RS Army for the execution of this crucial task: The expulsion of Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave. There will be no retreat when it comes to the Srebrenica enclave; we must advance. The enemy's life has to be made unbearable and their temporary stay in the enclave impossible so that they leave the enclave en masse as soon as possible, realising that they cannot survive there." My question to you, sir, is: Was this the policy as you knew it to be back then in 1994, pursuant to information that was issued by your then-commander, Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the significance of this information, if anything? If anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I will give you my own opinion. Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic ardently covered the rank of colonel. He kept complaining of how he was successfully commanding the brigade but was unable to obtain the rank of colonel, and this is something that he always said at meetings with the superior command. So I heard that General Mladic had told him: If, with your unit, namely the brigade, you enter Srebrenica, you will indeed be conferred the rank of colonel. So from this memo, one can see that this paper under item 1 actually indicates that this would ensue. So this is an information memorandum for the Main Staff in order to boost the morale of the troops and of me, myself, although we -- none of us believed in it at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I believe there may be some questions from Mr. Stojanovic's lawyer. I'm sure the Prosecution will have some questions and I've been given a note that the Colonel Jankovic document which was dated 13/7/2004 [sic] is D164 for identification purposes. That's all. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day. As I did for other witnesses, I have to tell you that during your stay in The Hague you are under oath, so do not tell anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.49 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
